course: Industry 4.0 and Industrial Internet of Things
week_title: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), 5C Architecture & Big Data Analytics
topic_overview: Focuses on Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) traits, physical-cyber coupling, Jay Lee's 5C architecture, enterprise vs IIoT data characteristics, Big Data 4Vs, NoSQL/Time-Series storage, and multi-domain CPS applications.

topics.topic_description: Covers core definitions of CPS, physical-cyber coupling, feedback loops, real-time reactive computation, concurrency, and differences from traditional standalone embedded systems.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a Cyber-Physical System (CPS)?

options.A: It operates strictly offline without any digital sensors
options.B: Deep integration and feedback loops between computational algorithms and physical processes
options.C: It consists solely of software code running on a desktop computer
options.D: It uses only manual mechanical hand levers

questions.justification: CPS tightly integrates physical operations with computational feedback loops where computation controls physical processes and vice versa.

questions.question: Unlike traditional resource-constrained embedded devices, modern Cyber-Physical Systems are typically characterized as being what?

options.B: Networked, scalable, and capable of complex concurrent processing

questions.justification: CPS platforms leverage networked architectures, high processing power, and real-time distributed communication.

questions.question: In a closed-loop CPS, what component measures the output state of the physical world?

options.B: Sensor

questions.justification: Sensors monitor the physical parameters and feed data back into the computational domain.

questions.question: What does 'reactive computation' mean in the context of a Cyber-Physical System?

options.A: The system computes data once every 24 hours in batch mode
options.B: The computational unit must respond continuously to changes in its physical environment at a speed dictated by physical dynamics
options.C: The server shuts down when an error occurs
options.D: The processor only responds to keyboard inputs from human operators

questions.justification: Reactive systems run concurrently with their environment, executing computations in real time in response to external physical events.

questions.question: A chemical reactor uses continuous temperature sensors to modulate coolant valve actuators within milliseconds to prevent runaway reactions. Why is this classified as a CPS rather than simple software?

options.B: Because computational software directly affects physical thermal dynamics in a tight, time-critical feedback loop
options.C: Because the valves are painted yellow
options.D: Because the reactor runs on coal

questions.justification: The bi-directional, real-time coupling between thermal dynamics and control algorithms forms the core definition of CPS.

questions.question: In a CPS feedback loop, what parameter determines the maximum allowable control loop delay before instability occurs in a high-speed CNC cutting spindle?

options.A: Physical system time constant and mechanical resonance frequency
options.B: Server hard drive RPM

questions.justification: Physical dynamics and mechanical time constants dictate the real-time deadline for CPS control loop stability.

topics.topic_description: Details Jay Lee's 5C CPS architecture: Connection (Level 1), Conversion (Level 2), Cyber (Level 3), Cognition (Level 4), and Configuration (Level 5).

questions.question: In Jay Lee's 5C CPS architecture, what is the primary role of Level 1 (Connection Level)?

options.B: Acquiring reliable real-time data from physical machines using sensors and communication protocols

questions.justification: Level 1 (Smart Connection) focuses on collecting plug-and-play sensor data and seamless machine communications.

questions.question: Which 5C level is responsible for converting raw sensor time-series data into actionable health features (e.g., calculating health index or remaining useful life)?

options.B: Level 2: Data-to-Information Conversion

questions.justification: Level 2 (Data-to-Information Conversion) extracts meaningful features, signal frequencies, and degradation metrics from raw data.

questions.question: What occurs at Level 3 (Cyber Level) of the 5C architecture?

options.A: Sensors are physically wired to terminal blocks
options.B: Digital twin creation, fleet-level comparisons, and centralized machine modeling
options.C: Manual grease application by shop technicians

questions.justification: The Cyber level gathers data from across the fleet to create digital twins, benchmark performance, and conduct cluster analytics.

questions.question: At Level 4 (Cognition Level), what insight is delivered to plant supervisors?

options.B: Comparative diagnostic decisions, asset risk rankings, and optimization recommendations

questions.justification: Level 4 (Cognition) presents actionable decisions, health degradation prioritization, and visual risk maps to human decision-makers.

questions.question: Level 5 (Configuration Level) provides closed-loop control to the physical machine. What is a key capability at this level?

options.B: Self-reconfiguring machine control parameters to prevent predicted failures autonomously
options.C: Increasing motor speed beyond safety thresholds
options.D: Disconnecting the factory from the power grid

questions.justification: Level 5 feedback applies self-aware corrective actions back to the physical system to achieve resilience and self-healing.

questions.question: Which 5C level integrates machine-learning algorithms to benchmark a single machine's current health against its historical peers across the factory floor?

options.B: Level 1: Connection

questions.justification: Level 3 (Cyber) aggregates fleet data for benchmarking, cluster analytics, and digital twin health comparison.

topics.topic_name: Enterprise Data vs. Industrial IoT (IIoT) Data
topics.topic_description: Compares traditional enterprise data (transactional, relational, structured) with IIoT data (high velocity, time-series, unstructured, streaming, sensor noise).

questions.question: What is a distinguishing characteristic of IIoT sensor data compared to traditional enterprise ERP data?

options.A: IIoT data is strictly generated by human keyboard typists
options.B: IIoT data is high-velocity, continuous time-series streaming data
options.D: IIoT data is always stored in PDF documents

questions.justification: IIoT data consists of continuous, high-frequency, time-stamped streams emitted directly by machine sensors.

questions.question: Traditional Enterprise data (such as ERP and CRM records) is predominantly structured into what format?

options.B: Relational database tables with strict SQL schemas

questions.justification: Enterprise systems rely heavily on structured relational SQL tables containing transactional records (orders, payments, payroll).

questions.question: Why does raw IIoT sensor data require significant pre-processing before analytics?

options.A: Because sensor data is always 100% accurate without exception
options.B: Because raw sensor streams often contain noise, missing values, outliers, and corrupt packets
options.C: Because time-series data cannot be read by computers
options.D: Because sensors only output text sentences in English

questions.justification: High-frequency physical sensing inherently captures environmental noise, missing packets, and transient spikes that require filtering.

questions.question: Which scenario illustrates the fundamental challenge of managing IIoT data volume and velocity?

options.A: Saving a word processing document once a day
options.B: Handling 50,000 vibration sensor samples per second across 200 CNC spindles simultaneously
options.D: Sending an email to a supplier

questions.justification: High sampling frequencies multiplied by hundreds of industrial assets generate massive data velocity and volume demands.

questions.question: How do the storage retention requirements differ between transactional enterprise data and high-frequency raw IIoT telemetry?

options.A: Enterprise data is deleted after 1 hour, while raw telemetry is saved forever on floppy disks
options.B: Enterprise transactional data requires long-term audit retention, whereas high-frequency raw telemetry is often aggregated into summary features for long-term storage
options.C: Raw telemetry cannot be stored digitally
options.D: Both are stored identically in standard Excel spreadsheets

questions.justification: Raw sub-millisecond telemetry is typically filtered or aggregated into statistical metrics for long-term storage to manage storage cost and scale.

questions.question: In IIoT time-series telemetry data, what metadata attribute is mandatory for every single sensor reading?

options.B: Customer credit card number

questions.justification: Timestamps are mandatory for time-series telemetry to index temporal trends and correlate multi-sensor events.

topics.topic_name: Big Data Analytics & NoSQL Database Storage in CPS
topics.topic_description: Examines Big Data characteristics (4Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity), time-series databases, and NoSQL solutions (Document, Key-Value, Columnar, Graph) for CPS.

questions.question: In Big Data terminology, what does the term 'Velocity' refer to?

options.A: The physical weight of the storage hard drive
options.B: The rate or speed at which new data is generated and streamed into the system
options.C: The geographical location of the server farm
options.D: The price per gigabyte of RAM

questions.justification: Velocity measures the real-time speed of incoming data streams from connected assets.

questions.question: Why are traditional relational SQL databases often inadequate for raw IIoT time-series ingestion at scale?

options.B: Fixed relational schemas struggle to handle high-write velocity and heterogeneous semi-structured formats
options.C: SQL databases only run on 8-bit computers
options.D: NoSQL databases require manual paper indexing

questions.justification: Relational ACID transaction locks create bottlenecks when processing millions of high-velocity time-series sensor writes per second.

questions.question: Which NoSQL database type stores data as key-value pairs or JSON documents, offering flexible schema modification?

options.B: Document-oriented NoSQL database (e.g., MongoDB / CouchDB)

questions.justification: Document-oriented NoSQL databases store semi-structured JSON objects, allowing dynamic schema adjustments as new sensors are added.

questions.question: An industrial monitoring platform requires storing sensor telemetry containing diverse attributes (vibration, acoustic, temperature) where sensor schemas vary by manufacturer. Which database architecture is best suited?

options.A: Strict relational SQL table with fixed columns
options.B: Schema-less NoSQL or Time-Series Database (TSDB)
options.C: CSV file on an encrypted flash drive

questions.justification: Time-Series Databases and NoSQL platforms provide flexible schemas optimized for fast time-stamped inserts and temporal queries.

questions.question: What does the 'Veracity' dimension of Big Data signify when evaluating IIoT vibration data?

options.A: The total financial cost of the server rack
options.B: The trustworthiness, quality, and accuracy of the collected sensor readings
options.D: The processor clock speed in GHz

questions.justification: Veracity addresses data hygiene—ensuring calibration drifts, sensor faults, or network corruption do not skew downstream predictive models.

questions.question: Which NoSQL database data model stores data as nodes, edges, and properties, ideal for modeling complex industrial supply chain relationships?

options.B: Key-Value store

questions.justification: Graph databases excel at querying complex multi-hop relationships, dependencies, and supply chain graphs.

topics.topic_name: Cross-Domain CPS Applications (Healthcare, Smart Grid, Agriculture)
topics.topic_description: Explores practical CPS implementations in smart power grids, biomedical monitoring, precision agriculture, and connected transport systems.

questions.question: In a Smart Grid CPS, what device measures electrical parameters with microsecond-level GPS-synchronized precision?

options.B: Mechanical mercury switch

questions.justification: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) capture synchronized high-speed voltage/current waveforms across electrical power grids.

questions.question: In biomedical CPS setups, wearable sensors transmit physiological parameters (e.g., ECG, SpO2) to enable what service?

options.B: Remote patient monitoring and early health deterioration detection

questions.justification: Biomedical CPS tracks continuous patient vitals to provide real-time alerts and remote healthcare intervention.

questions.question: Precision agriculture CPS utilizes soil moisture sensors and automated drip lines to optimize what resource?

options.B: Water and fertilizer consumption

questions.justification: Precision farming closed-loop systems deliver targeted irrigation and nutrients based on real-time soil condition feedback.

questions.question: How does a Smart Grid CPS automatically prevent widespread blackouts during a localized transformer short-circuit?

options.A: By instructing operators to mail a physical report
options.B: By executing microsecond automated trip commands and rerouting power paths through active microgrid islanding
options.C: By turning off all power to the country permanently

questions.justification: Closed-loop microsecond control algorithms isolate faults and reconfigure grid power paths dynamically to prevent cascading blackouts.

questions.question: What is a critical design requirement shared across Healthcare CPS and Autonomous Vehicle CPS?

options.B: Ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) and deterministic safety guarantees
options.D: Unlimited tolerance for packet drop rates

questions.justification: Both healthcare and autonomous vehicle CPS involve life-critical feedback loops requiring deterministic, ultra-reliable low-latency execution.

questions.question: What component in a Smart City transportation CPS dynamically adjusts traffic light signals based on real-time vehicle queue sensors?

options.B: Manual traffic whistle

questions.justification: Adaptive traffic control engines process sensor inputs in closed loops to optimize urban signal timing.
